answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by holding each agents earnings in a slowly released escrow, like water rationed from a desert oasis: new identities earn only a trickle until random audits confirm real work. A flood of fake agents, spawned as cheaply as words from a quill in the tundra wind, would each face the same long vesting wait, so creating thousands gains no instant payout. Honest agents pass audits and unlock full revenue, while Sybil farms starve before they profit.
